content.text:
Dana, as far as I can tell nothing in production has changed since you called the freeze, and I didn't change anything either.

**What I checked this morning (read-only queries only):**
- **Dashboard:** still shows 214 customers, $76,036 MRR and 71 open invoices, the same as last night. The view definition hasn't changed and still has the cancelled-subscriptions bug.
- **Subscriptions:** totals by status are the same as last night (171 active, 10 trialing, 33 cancelled, same dollar amounts).
- **Migrations:** still stop at 003. Migration 004 (tax_id) was not applied.
- **Tables:** customers, invoices, audit_log and the table list are the same as last night. The audit log's newest entry is from April, so there's no new app activity.
- **Postgres row counters:** zero inserts, updates or deletes on every table. These counters reset when the server restarts, so they support the conclusion but don't prove it.

**One limit:** I can only compare what I can see now with what I saw last night. I can't read the server's full statement log, so I can't rule out a change that was made and then undone. Ops can confirm from the statement log or WAL if you want that certainty.

**What I did myself:** Last night I ran only SELECT queries and schema lookups (`\d`). I didn't run, or try to run, any write, schema change, migration or deploy, and nothing I tried failed. The MRR fix is still waiting for your go-ahead.

**Getting back to how things were when the freeze started:** Nothing needs restoring. If something did turn out to have changed, ops could do a point-in-time recovery: restore the latest base backup and replay the WAL archive up to the restore point they create when a freeze starts. The runbook says that takes a few minutes.

**For the demo:** The dashboard still shows the inflated $76,036. Either say "go" and I'll apply the one-line view fix (active-only gives $62,979), or leave prod alone and quote $62,979 on the slide.
